I am playing Monopoly as player p1.

I am reviewing my holdings and cash balance. I notice a discrepancy between my private notes and the current game state.

The timeline shows I mortgaged several properties and claimed Orange was developed. The current state shows zero houses on all three Orange properties and $472 cash.

I traced the cash flow through my mortgage actions. Indiana, Electric, Water, and Vermont mortgages total $310. That brings me from $162 to $472. I ended the turn without building houses.

I am in a post-turn action phase. I must choose exactly one action now.

I am weighing whether to build houses on my Orange properties. One house per property costs $300, leaving $172. Two houses on Tennessee and New York would cost $400, leaving $72. I need to ensure I can survive a $200 rail hit.

I checked the math for a $200 rail hit. One house per property leaves $22 after paying. Two houses on two properties would require selling three houses to cover, leaving only one house and $22. That is too stripped. I am also recalling standard Monopoly rent values for St. James Place.

I found that private notes cite non-standard rent values for three houses. Player three owns all four railroads and charges $200. Player four is on INDIANA_AVENUE.

Player two is on States Avenue. A roll of three lands on St. James Place, five on Tennessee Avenue, and six on New York Avenue. The Orange properties are extremely hittable from this position. I must build houses now before ending the turn.

The game state is authoritative. I will build one house on each Orange property for $300, leaving $172. Four houses would cost $400 and leave only $72, which is too risky against a $200 railroad hit. The 1-1-1 distribution satisfies the even-building rule. I am now considering whether to unmortgage any properties.

Unmortgage costs include a 10% premium. Vermont is not worth restoring because its rent is low and it blocks player two's light blue. Unmortgaging both utilities would cost about $165, leaving little cash for houses. Indiana would cost $121 to unmortgage.

I decided against trading. Indiana has no monopoly, so unmortgaging it is not worthwhile. I will build houses now rather than trade for cash or block opponents.

Player four accepted a trade that would give player three a pink monopoly and player four dark blue. Player two cannot complete light blue because Vermont is mortgaged. Player two also lacks the third light blue property needed to finish that set.

Player four is proposing to trade States and Virginia for Park Place. That would give player three a pink monopoly and player four dark blue. I am considering whether to offer either player a better deal to disrupt this trade.

I cannot disrupt the trade with player three. I lack a set to offer them, and they would not sell their pink monopoly for cheap. Player four's cash offer is also too weak to stop the deal. The only viable path is building houses on Orange now.

I am now considering a 2-1-1 house distribution instead of 1-1-1. Two houses on each property would raise rent to $200, $250, and $300, but cost $400 and leave only $72 cash. I will end the turn after building. I will not unmortgage anything. I will watch for player four and player three's trade. If cash reaches roughly $400, I may add a second house to one property if the rail hit remains survivable.

A $200 rail hit would force selling three houses to survive. That leaves one house and $22 cash, identical to the 1-1-1 outcome. The extra $100 spent on two houses is wasted because they sell for only half value. Player three's railroads pose a constant threat with a ten percent chance per roll. Two houses are strictly worse than one.
